title: Embedding retrieval: cosine top-k and MMR re-ranking
hints: Cosine similarity of unit vectors is a dot product: normalize the documents once, normalize the query, then sims = docs_n @ q_n is the whole score vector. Guard the norm with np.maximum(norm, eps) so a zero row stays zero instead of becoming nan.
np.argpartition(-sims, k - 1)[:k] finds the k largest in O(n) but in no particular order; sort just those k by score to return them ranked.

MMR is greedy: start with the most relevant document, then repeatedly add the unselected document maximizing lam * sim(q, d) - (1 - lam) * max_{s in selected} sim(d, s). Keep a running vector of each document's maximum similarity to the selected set and update it with np.maximum after every pick, so each step is O(n d).
